title: Capacity commit approval heuristics and scaling contract
creator: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:
We need a repeatable, developer-friendly provisioning lifecycle for dedicated capacity that ties a customer’s capacity commitment (throughput commit) to an autoscaling contract and approval heuristics. The goal is to reduce manual triage during intake, make approval decisions predictable, and embed safety guardrails so committed throughput meets SLOs without overprovisioning fleet resources.

Goals:
- Define approval heuristics that map commitment size, historical usage, and risk signals to an approval lane (auto-approve, concierge review, or executive signoff).
- Define a machine-actionable scaling contract that encodes committed throughput, minimum/failback capacity, cooldown windows, and cost attribution.
- Produce console flows and API endpoints to accept requests, surface risk indicators, and display a clear expected timeline and commit terms to customers.
- Ensure autoscale policy templates implement committed throughput guarantees while preserving headroom for burst and graceful degradation.
- Provide telemetry and dashboards for observability (provisioning SLA, post-provision utilization, and cost-per-token reconciliation).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Intake API: a new /provisioning/requests endpoint that accepts commitment metadata (expected tokens/sec, window, duration, legal-tier) and returns an estimated decision lane and TTL for final decision.
2) Approval heuristics: documented rules and a prototype service implementing the heuristics with deterministic outputs for common patterns (low usage, new account, high-variance bursts).
3) Scaling contract: schema (JSON) that includes fields: committed_rps, min_guarantee_rps, burst_buffer_pct, cooldown_minutes, fallback_model_tier, billing_profile_id. Backwards-compatible with existing billing ledger.
4) Console UX: intake form, risk banner, and SLA summary + timeline; can request manual review.
5) Autoscale templates: three templates (conservative, balanced, aggressive) that map to kernel/batching tuning and target percentiles for p50/p95 latency.
6) Telemetry: dashboard with provisioning_request_count, time_to_approve, post_provision_utilization_24h, percent_overcommit_events, and cost_reconciliation_error.
7) Playbook: runbook for ops including rollback steps, decommit flow, and emergency throttle.

Work already done / links:
- Confluence spec (draft): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/987654321/Provisioning+Lifecycle+Blueprint (draft)
- Prototype heuristics service (PR): https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioning/pull/178
- Console intake mockups: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBCdeZ_mockups
- Billing mapping doc: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1BillingMapping_2026
- Provisioning dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/Provisioning/requests

Design / trade-offs noted:
- Auto-approve threshold: we debated a hard token/sec cutoff vs. a probabilistic risk score. Decided to start with deterministic rules for predictability (easier for sales/legal) and iterate to risk-scores in v2.
- Min_guarantee_rps vs. billing: some customers expect hard guarantees; others accept best-effort. The contract will express both a guaranteed minimum and a billed committed amount (can differ) to allow flexible commercial terms.
- Autoscale conservatism: we will bias towards a conservative template for first 30 days post-provision to avoid noisy neighbor incidents, then shift to balanced as signals mature.

Progress updates / comments:
- 2026-02-28: Scoping workshop with Eng (Liam), SRE (Marta), Sales Eng (Rohit). Action: define 6 canonical request archetypes and sample telemetry.
- 2026-03-03: Heuristics prototype returns deterministic lanes for 80% of sampled historical requests. Found edge case with accounts that have high variance across regions; added region-aware rule.
- 2026-03-07: Console mocks reviewed by Design; risk banner copy needs legal review. Added label `needs-legal-copy`.
- 2026-03-10: Billing confirmed schema can accept billing_profile_id as a key for mapping to committed invoices. Eng will add reconciliation hooks.
- 2026-03-12: Ops playbook draft complete; includes emergency decommit path and matrix for when to apply emergency throttle.

Open questions / blockers:
- Legal signoff on SLA wording (affects exact guarantee language). Owner: Maria Delgado (Legal). Blocked until 2026-03-20 if no reply.
- Integration with legacy reservation ledger (edge-case customers still on old contracts). Requires a migration adapter from Billing.
- Autoscale runtime knobs: need runtime support for min_guarantee_rps and burst_buffer_pct in serving runtime v1.19 (ENG-22498).

Next steps (2-week plan):
- Finalize heuristics ruleset and publish deterministic test vectors (ENG-231010).
- Implement intake API prototype and wire up console form for internal staging (ENG-231011).
- Legal review of SLA copy and finalize billing mapping (owner: Maria Delgado / Billing).
- QA run: provision 3 pilot customers and monitor first 72 hours for p95 latency and cost reconciliation.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Overcommitting fleet leading to p95 latency degradation. Mitigation: conservative autoscale template, automated fallback to fallback_model_tier, and rate-limited decommit policy.
- Risk: Sales unhappy with slow approvals. Mitigation: define an auto-approve lane for low-risk requests (<X rps, >3 months history) and a concierge lane SLA of 48 hours.

Success metrics (post-launch 30/90 days):
- Median time to approve request < 24 hours for auto-approve lane; < 72 hours for concierge.
- Percentage of provisioning requests where realized utilization >= 60% of committed after 7 days (target 70%).
- No more than 3 production incidents attributable to provisioning overcommit in first 90 days.

Contacts / stakeholders:
- PM lead: Asha Patel (creator)
- Eng lead: Liam Chen (assignee)
- SRE: Marta Kovacs
- Billing: Priya Nair
- Legal: Maria Delgado

Notes for handoff: include JSON schema for scaling contract in API repo, a migration adapter task for legacy ledger, and a short playbook for Sales Eng to explain commit semantics to customers.
